rationale: A wins because it knows where the floorboards end. Its line, "Without that person this angle does not exist," is the kind of discipline founders need before they start pitching vapor; B's "Discord undercuts Apple and Google" turns a fee benchmark into a named fight the supplied facts do not actually establish. B is useful, but A is cleaner, tougher, and less eager to decorate the facts.
gaps_in_A: "right before an IPO" overstates the timing. The update says Discord is reportedly preparing for an IPO, not that this launch is immediately pre-filing.
"Paying for the room, not the creator" is a strong lens, but the update does not yet prove community membership is materially different from paid creator content. It needs that caveat sharper.
"Nitro-style subscriptions" brings in outside Discord context. It is framed as missing proof, not a core claim, but it still reaches beyond the supplied update.
The trend angle and server-owner angle share territory around paid community operators; they are distinct enough, but not by a mile.
gaps_in_B: "Discord undercuts Apple and Google" invents named antagonists. The update only says 10% is below the 30% app-store standard.
"ads, Nitro" smuggles in revenue lines not supplied in the update. That is exactly how a clean IPO angle gets mud on it.
"it won't say how much they'll make" turns absence of data into an accusation. The facts say no creator-earnings data is available because the program is new.
"gambling- or loot-box-adjacent" is a brand-safety antenna, but it is not grounded in the update. It feels bolted on from generic gaming-platform worry.
